summary.text: The Walker circulation is a model of air in the lower tropical atmosphere moving in a closed loop along east–west and vertical directions.
It is caused by differences in how heat is spread between ocean and land, and is linked to high pressure over the eastern Pacific and low pressure over Indonesia.
It weakens during El Niño, when the Pacific temperature gradient and the easterly winds both drop, and strengthens during La Niña.

facts.label: Named after
facts.value: Gilbert Walker, who discovered the Southern Oscillation

facts.label: Pressure pattern
facts.value: High over the eastern Pacific, low over Indonesia

facts.label: Sinking-air region
facts.value: Bjerknes called it the arid zone

items.prompt: An El Niño develops and the easterly winds across the Pacific slacken. What happens to the Walker circulation?

options.label: It grows stronger
It grows weaker
It flips for good
It stays the same

items.explain: The Walker circulation is weaker during El Niño, when the temperature gradient across the Pacific and the easterlies are both reduced.

items.prompt: Easterly winds cool the sea surface in the eastern Pacific, sharpening the east–west heat contrast. What happens to those winds next?

options.label: They weaken
They turn north
They stop
They intensify

items.explain: In this coupled ocean-atmosphere feedback, the stronger heat contrast intensifies the easterly winds across the basin.

items.prompt: Gilbert Walker found that weather relationships could be entirely different depending on the season. How did he set up his analysis?

options.label: He split each year into four three-month periods
He averaged all his data over whole years
He studied only the monsoon months
He threw out the seasonal data entirely

items.explain: Walker judged a one-year time scale unsuitable, so he broke his analysis into December–February, March–May, June–August and September–November.

items.prompt: Why did Gilbert Walker publish the correlations he found unimportant, not just the strong ones?

options.label: To prove that sunspots drive the weather
Because his editors demanded full data
To steer others away from links that did not exist
To make his reports long enough for funding

items.explain: He published all his findings, important and unimportant, to dissuade researchers from focusing on correlations that did not exist.

items.prompt: What sets up the Walker circulation in the first place?

options.label: Uneven heating of ocean and land
The pull of Earth's magnetic field
Tides raised by the Moon
Heat leaking from Earth's core

items.explain: The circulation is caused by differences in heat distribution between ocean and land.

items.prompt: In northern summer the Walker circulation gives the equatorial Pacific easterly surface winds and cool water in the east, but gives the Indian Ocean westerly winds. Where would you expect the Indian Ocean's cooler surface water?

options.label: In the east, as in the Pacific
Spread evenly across the basin
In the west, unlike the Pacific
Only at the very centre of the basin

items.explain: The Pacific and Atlantic have cool surface water in the east in northern summer, while in the Indian Ocean cooler surface temperatures prevail only in the west.
